marks.description: Christ as the center of our life calls us to return to our first and only love—the One we promised to follow with undivided heart. Rooted in His love, we learn from Him how to love in truth and mercy. Guided by the Spirit, we seek each day to live and act asking, “What would Jesus do?

         Steps of the Examen

     and near.

     welcoming, constant.

     every moment of your day.

     grace connected to the SPC Mark you are focusing 
      on.

              moments.”

preliminaries:
Consciousness Examen trains us to live in constant awareness of God’s loving presence, helps us recognize the Holy Spirit's movement in our daily lives, and guides us to imitate Christ.
This Examen Guide integrates 12 Marks that embody key dimensions of our SPC identity and apostolic calling with the Directives of the 49th General Chapter, made concrete in the Ten Commitments for Communal Actions.
When practiced faithfully, this Examen helps us live out our SPC spirituality and deepen our sense of identity as consecrated women, fostering attentiveness to God’s presence, discernment in our daily choices, and concrete expressions of our charism, values, and mission in personal, communal, and apostolic life.
The Love of Christ impels us.
2 Corinthians 5:14
The M.A.R.K.S. Examen Guide M – Mindful of God’s Presence
A – Appreciate with Gratitude
R – Review and Recognize Movements K – Kindle a Heart Open to God’s Mercy S – Surrender and Serve
Steps of the Examen
M – Mindful of God’s Presence
“Be still and know that I am God.” (Psalm 46:10)
Quiet yourself and become aware that God is here and near.
Feel His loving gaze upon you — gentle, welcoming, constant.
Remember that He has been with you through every moment of your day.
Read the assigned Scripture text and beg for the grace connected to the SPC Mark you are focusing on.
Becoming mindful invites us to rest in God’s nearness before we recall anything else.
“Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good.” (Psalm 136:1)
Let your heart recall today’s blessings — big or small.
People who showed you kindness… beauty you noticed… strength you received.
Speak to God with a grateful heart.
“Thank You for being present in these moments.”
Gratitude helps us see that nothing in our day was outside God’s loving care.
Movements
“Were not our hearts burning within us?” (Luke 24:32)
Gently walk through your day with Jesus beside you.
Read and reflect on today’s assigned question, based on your chosen SPC Mark and its weekly theme.
As you review your experiences in light of the reflection question, notice where and how God’s presence, love, or invitations were revealed to you.
This is not self-judgment, but awareness — seeing how God, through His love, moved through your day.
“Abide in Me, and I in you.” (John 15:4)
Allow the Lord to soften and open your heart where there has been hurt, resistance, or failure.
Bring to Him any sorrow, missteps, or relationships in need of healing.
Ask Jesus to kindle in you a humble, repentant heart, ready to begin anew in His mercy.
What is He gently asking you to improve,
renew, or make right — within yourself or in your relationships today?
Start anew by renewing our friendship with God and seeking His guidance to grow, repair, and live more fully in His love.
S – Surrender and Serve
“Here I am, Lord; I come to do Your will.” (Psalm 40:8)
Carry with you God’s assurance, along with the inspirations and invitations received during the examen.
Hold in your heart the SPC Mark you are focusing on this week.
Entrust the rest of the day — or the day to come
— to God’s mercy and guidance.
Conclude with a personal prayer of commitment to love and serve God with renewed faith, hope, and charity.
The Examen ends not in introspection but in mission — to live as one marked by God’s love.
TEN COMMITMENTS FOR COMMUNAL ACTIONS
49TH General Chapter/Council of Province 2025
We commit to center our life fully in Christ by intensifying our personal and communal prayer, faithfully safeguarding sacred times of prayer and rest, and ensuring that our hearts remain attentive, recollected, and available to God.
(PRAYER LIFE)
We commit to live Christ’s way--chaste, poor and obedient—by intentionally embracing simplicity, exercising prudence in our choices of personal items, brands, and places of recreation, and accountability for initiatives and decisions. Each month, we will include a Simplicity Check in our examen or community spiritual conversations, conduct a semestral community sorting and sharing of unused items with those most in need. (LIFE OF CONSECRATION)
We commit to nurture fraternal communion, by setting aside time for regular simple recreation, relaxation, and friendship-building activities that strengthen bonds, cultivate joy, and deepen our sense of belonging to one another, thus making our communities our primary place of mission and a school of love. (FRATERNAL LIFE)
We commit to build communities where spaces of welcome and dialogue are created, by consciously using inclusive language and communication practices so that no Sister ever feels left out, unseen, or unheard. (INTERCULTURALITY)
We commit to live synodality and reciprocity in our communities, ensuring that every voice is heard in matters that affect our life and mission through consultative and participatory decision-making, valuing each Sister’s gifts, and sharing responsibilities fairly. (CO-RESPONSIBILITY)
We commit to journey together in mission by collaborating with our lay partners, local Church, and the wider Church community in the areas of justice, peace, and ecological concerns, practicing transparency and accountability as we walk together in service. (SYNODALITY)
As a community, we commit to pursue holistic formation for all our Sisters that includes mentoring and succession planning, transition program for aging and ailing Sisters, responsible use of new technologies and artificial intelligence, sustainable environment stewardship (Laudato Si) so that our life and mission remain life-giving, relevant, and faithful to the Church and the Book of Life. (FORMATION)
We commit to remain faithful to our mission while responding creatively to our call to be prophetic witnesses by taking a clear Congregational stand—rooted in prayer, discernment, and sentire cum ecclesia (actively feeling, thinking, and acting with the Church) against threats to life, human trafficking, graft and corruption, injustice, abuse of power, disinformation, and all forms of ecological destruction, actively promoting life, truth, justice, peace, and the integrity of creation. (MISSIONARY ZEAL)
As a community, we commit to cultivate a spirituality of Visitation, by reviewing internal and external structures of our ministries through prayerful discernment so that we remain truly present to those entrusted to us, promote lay empowerment, and ensure our lifestyle reflects mercy, simplicity, justice, and the nearness of Christ. (MISSION OF PROXIMITY)
As a community, we commit to strengthen vocation promotion and formation for mission, staying informed on social and ecclesial issues, immersion in mission areas, practicing responsible digital formation, and offering programs that build spiritual depth, pastoral skills, Justice, Peace, and Integrity of Creation (JPIC) awareness, and ethical responsibility. (FORMATION)
